newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currencies end off, June marks on new lows.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currencies end off, June marks on new lows.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures closed lower, with June marks and yen establishing contract low settlements on heavy selling at the close, floor traders said.
"It was a big day for the dollar, but I wouldn't go home short currencies," one currency floor analyst said. "Now it's time to lighten the load."
However, most traders anticipate only a slim retracement -- possibly to the upper end of Wednesday's pit ranges.
"Everyday there is just more and more pressure," he said.
June marks set a contract low of $0.5815 as the dollar/mark rallied to 1.7270, and June yen established its latest contract low at $0.007951, or about 127.00 spot.

While June yen has been hitting a string of contract lows on GLOBEX and during pit trade, June marks until Wednesday morning had failed to break the previous contract low set at $0.5840. June marks' resiliency in the face of continued yen selling led some traders to look for a brief mark bounce.
However, selling pressures emerged in the pit as hedge funds bought the dollar during the day with the same gusto as overseas investors overnight, currency analysts said.
Several currency analysts said dollar/mark's rally through 1.7230 or about $0.5831 in June marks sparked buying from hedge fund and model-driven asset allocators, they said.

June marks' initial drop below the previous contract low of $0.5840 was based on positive U.S. interest rate differentials, coupled with diminished expectations for central bank intervention, said Rob Fullem, a currency analyst at NatWest Securities.
"There has just been a huge reduction, probably overly, in expectations on intervention," he said.

Fullem said intervention fears could resurface next week when U.S. February international trade figures are released on April 17. The U.S. trade deficit numbers could coincide with the Clinton administration's review of the 1995 U.S.-Japan trade pact.
The administration's review, which will be released in mid-April, is expected to show that many of the goals envisaged by U.S. industry and U.S. trade officials have not been met.
"The intervention issue could come back," Fullem said.
"(U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert) Rubin has mentioned the trade picture," he said.
In January, the U.S. trade gap grew 21.1 percent to $12.71 billion, the highest in nearly a decade.
Aside from late heavy selling in yen and marks, floor sources said funds were active sellers in Canadian dollars.

At the end of pit trade, June yen was off $0.000042 at $0.007961, marks were off $0.0040 at $0.5822, Swiss francs fell $0.0035 to $0.6806, sterling lost $0.0076 to $1.6174, Can dollars were off $0.0013 at $0.7224, Aussie dollars were up $0.0028 at $0.7832 and Mexican pesos were up $0.000125 at $0.122825.
